PASS for the two scoped additions, relative to the exact actual-ample G0 grant. This does not accept full-original P16.5. Author117 candidate=false and canonical114 INCONCLUSIVE remain unchanged. The passage indexed −1 binds the task grant and is excluded from the external-premise array.

The retained hypotheses suffice for every application: the original smooth integral projective X is normal and geometrically unibranch; all bundles receiving G0 applications are actual ample rational bundles on that same X. Arbitrary cardinality is retained. Compactness arguments use nets and subnets, not sequential compactness. No nonample closure, envelope or equation theorem is obtained by relabelling an ample theorem.

Sections 1–2: the center-frame construction gives literal tensor compatibility and the generating-section identity on points of nongeneric support as well. Upward rational rounding followed by the additional positive shift produces a directed decreasing single net, including at common poles. Multiplication by generators of actual ample differences preserves each scalar exactly. A generically finite FS function on an auxiliary ample bundle belongs to its genuine cone by adjoining constant floors and applying fixed-ample decreasing closure. The finite-maximum construction uses admissible triples and actual sections of L+δH; it does not require that bundle itself to be ample. The finite-polytope computation includes zero slopes, opposite slopes, the minimum at infinity and infinite section logarithms. Its rational vertices give actual product sections. Commutation of the two infima establishes the homogeneous endpoint without nested nonample closure. The ray decomposition is valid at every point: the corrected auxiliary parameter 0<a<s<t0 propagates a pole along the entire ray; finite rays admit the required supporting line.

Section 3: openness, effective-class approximation and numerical ampleness construct actual A=L−O(D), including numerically trivial twists of big bundles. For a homogeneous dominated function, compactness of {σ=−1} gives the requisite tail inequalities. Normal section division constructs quotient functions everywhere. Their net need not decrease; the proof correctly uses rescaling into one normalized actual ample cone and compactness instead. The divisorial limit is explicitly h−σ, and common-ample determination gives all-point equality and uniqueness. The homogeneous decomposition and finite maxima then reconstruct the entire dominated cone, not merely its section-generated part. Order reflection, normalized compactness, fixed-reference decreasing closure and envelopes follow through the proved bijection. The empty-envelope convention is kept outside the generically finite cone.

Section 4: the actual frame identity has the correct plus sign, h_L=h_A+log|f|. The collar construction establishes the already-glued, continuous, rational, actual-ample contact antecedent before invoking G0. The thresholds in (21) are C_j. Compactness of the outer strip gives an entire admissible tail; it does not assert uniform convergence to a discontinuous endpoint. The indispensable identity is w=RΦ+Rh_0+M+1. Thus independent generated nets with the same endpoint have the same global collar endpoint and the same local products. Real weights, harmonic frame changes and different collars are covered by the stated comparisons. Mixed strict-winning locality can be checked by expanding sums of maxima into finitely many branches and then polarizing; positivity comes from the ample mixed measures. The weighted pairing has the stated test-minus-zero order.

The polar estimate is sufficient. Integration by parts bounds each normalized telescoping term by one, giving capacity decay n/t. Layer-cake integration retains t^n. For α<1/(n+1), the resulting integral for χ(a) converges. The same construction applied to a quotient potential removes its own poles. Mixed finite-energy integrability therefore removes the divisor and quotient poles without imposing a separate support condition. The increasing restricted products are finite Radon measures. Their construction precedes target selection; equality with the ample products, raw mass A^n, and mixed and weighted decreasing-net limits are consequences of locality and pole removal.

Sections 5–6: the constructed mixed products give E_D(u)=E_A(Q_Du). The target condition uses the uniquely retained quotient and requires mass A^n; it does not require integrability of σ. Normalized coercivity, compactness, lower semicontinuity of J, target-integral continuity and energy upper semicontinuity produce an actual maximizer. Both continuous derivative signs identify its already constructed measure with the target. Comparison and uniqueness transfer through the order bijection.

For every genuine bounded reference change, τ=σ+χ with χ a bounded genuine ample potential, including discontinuous χ. The dominated cones coincide. The common-floor inequalities and Borel strict-winning locality establish operator independence for arbitrary endpoints of the associated nonpluripolar construction; finite-energy endpoints retain full mass. The mixed cocycle gives E_τ(u)=E_D(u)−E_D(τ), and consequently D_τ(μ)=D_D(μ)−E_D(τ)+∫χ dμ. Boundedness makes the last term finite. The finite-energy spaces, intrinsic target classes and maximizers therefore coincide. For continuous variations, the common retained quotient and obstacle cone give the same outer-energy shift. The varying-mass family in Section 6.2 correctly prevents extending this conclusion to different singularity types.

Sections 7–8: the full-divisor constants cone follows from the ε-scaled ample evaluation bound, followed by all-point determination. Its local weight on the divisor complement is a unit logarithm plus a constant, so its positive-degree products and nonpluripolar extension are zero.

For an arbitrary actual numerical-zero L, the defining single net can likewise be embedded and normalized in εA. Compact evaluation bounds squeeze every divisorial value to its generic constant; ample determination gives equality everywhere. Conversely, generating powers of the actual ample bundles L+εA provide the required numerical approximation even when L has no sections. The endpoint metric remains on L.

The numerical-zero operator is independently constructed. The canonical metric is the actual metric difference (H+L)−H. Continuous dpsh products exist independently of this decomposition. Their signed ample expansion cancels because the two numerical classes agree and n≥1. The separate positive local approximations h_L+εh_A decrease uniformly on compact frame neighborhoods and have actual raw masses ε^n A^n. The common collar compares them with every bounded decreasing generated local approximation having the same endpoint. Thus the generated-local operator agrees with the independently constructed zero continuous product. No arbitrary-current density assertion is used.

All constant metrics consequently have zero mixed energy and finite energy. Every original continuous variation has feasible constants and zero outer derivative. The only positive target of zero mass is zero; every constant metric attains it, and the entire genuine cone is unique modulo constants. The section-divisor intersection argument gives h^0(mL)≤1 and hence volume zero. No probability normalization or zero-mass domination principle is introduced.

Sections 9–11 remain limited constructions and diagnostics. The ambient envelopes are actual ample-ambient functions; their unresolved nonample membership and volume equations are not certified. The semiample zero-mass obstruction and the extended-valued flattening counterexample are valid. The latter does not invalidate BE’s finite-continuous-metric flattening argument, whose comparison functions have finite values.

Fresh public evidence was obtained from [BJ v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4), [Fujino–Miyamoto v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2101.00806v1), [BE v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3), [CLD v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2) and the cited Stacks tags. Public rendered coordinates, with zero-based PDF pages, are: premises 0–1, BJ L515–528@P9, L570–628@P10–11, L1033–1045@P18 and L10983@P135; premise 4, L1588–1612@P26. The literal Definition 4.1 was also checked at L3142–3146@P44. Premise 2: statement L47–52@P1 and complete proof L179–303@P3–4. Premise 3: Stacks 01Q3 L23–67. Premise 5: BE L3812–3852@P47 and L3892–3908@P48–49; premise 6: L4259–4532@P54–57. BE v3 has arXiv stamp 8 January 2021. Premise 7: CLD v2, stamped 25 July 2025, L14836–14922@P210–211 and L35424–35439@P500. Premise 8: Stacks 0AG0 L24–29, with 0AFZ L22–24 inspected. Premise 9: 0BX5 L24–35, with the pertinent 01KA, 01KF, 01KZ and 01L0 proof units inspected. The complete pertinent printed units were checked; recursive Berkovich, intersection-theoretic, Birkar and commutative-algebra foundations were not independently reproved.

Harmless clarifications: in Section 4.2, “nonzero outside the divisor” should mean not identically zero there; additional zeros are allowed and only containment of Z in the pole set is needed. In (42), I_A must be explicitly probability-normalized for the displayed factor A^n. The transcribed BE Lemma 8.6 expansion needs a minus between the two curvature terms; the preceding curvature-difference identity and the absolute-value bound are unchanged. The completed paper already correctly handles the smaller pole parameter and empty feasible envelopes. No substantial repair of the scoped argument is required.

passages.statement: For a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, analytification is compact Hausdorff, and every line bundle’s canonical trivial metric and global section norms into [0,1] are continuous.

For a projective variety over an algebraically closed field, N^1(X) is finite dimensional, the ample cone is open, and the big cone is the interior of the closed cone generated by effective R-Cartier divisor classes.

passages.statement: On a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, if B is an actual rational bundle, E an effective rational Cartier divisor, and φ a generically finite Fubini–Study function in B satisfying φ≤log||s_E||+O(1), dividing its sections yields an all-point Fubini–Study function in B−E, equal to φ−log||s_E|| away from E (BJ v4, Lemma 2.23).

On a projective scheme over a complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation, every psh metric on a semiample rational bundle in BE’s fixed-bundle sense admits decreasing smooth semipositive regularization; convergence to a continuous endpoint is uniform (BE v3, Theorem 7.14).
passages.quote: Every psh metric φ on a semiample Q-line bundle L is psh-regularizable.

passages.statement: On an n-dimensional projective scheme over a complete valued field, continuous psh-regularizable rational-bundle metrics have unique symmetric multiadditive positive mixed Radon products of fundamental-cycle intersection mass, continuous from uniform to weak convergence. These products extend independently of decomposition to continuous dpsh metrics as symmetric multilinear signed Radon products (BE v3, Theorem 8.4, Proposition 8.5 and the extension preceding Example 8.11).

premises: For a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, analytification is compact Hausdorff, and every line bundle’s canonical trivial metric and global section norms into [0,1] are continuous.

For a projective variety over an algebraically closed field, N^1(X) is finite dimensional, the ample cone is open, and the big cone is the interior of the closed cone generated by effective R-Cartier divisor classes.

On a complete normal variety over an algebraically closed field, an R-Cartier divisor L is ample if and only if L^{dim Z}·Z>0 for every positive-dimensional closed subvariety Z (Fujino–Miyamoto v1, Theorem 1.4).
On a quasi-compact scheme with an ample invertible sheaf A, every finite-type quasi-coherent sheaf F has F⊗A^m globally generated for all sufficiently large integers m (Stacks 01Q3).

On a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, if B is an actual rational bundle, E an effective rational Cartier divisor, and φ a generically finite Fubini–Study function in B satisfying φ≤log||s_E||+O(1), dividing its sections yields an all-point Fubini–Study function in B−E, equal to φ−log||s_E|| away from E (BJ v4, Lemma 2.23).

On a projective scheme over a complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation, every psh metric on a semiample rational bundle in BE’s fixed-bundle sense admits decreasing smooth semipositive regularization; convergence to a continuous endpoint is uniform (BE v3, Theorem 7.14).

On an n-dimensional projective scheme over a complete valued field, continuous psh-regularizable rational-bundle metrics have unique symmetric multiadditive positive mixed Radon products of fundamental-cycle intersection mass, continuous from uniform to weak convergence. These products extend independently of decomposition to continuous dpsh metrics as symmetric multilinear signed Radon products (BE v3, Theorem 8.4, Proposition 8.5 and the extension preceding Example 8.11).

On boundaryless analytic spaces over a complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation, logarithms of analytic units are smooth with zero Hessian, and the continuous dpsh product construction against closed positive currents is invariant under addition of such harmonic terms (CLD v2, §§18.1.2 and 8.8.5).
